meaning: AWS's managed Kubernetes service. AWS runs the control plane, and you run your pods on nodes in your own account.
A countable resource beyond CPU and memory that a node advertises and a pod claims in whole units, such as nvidia.com/gpu.
The state of a pod that no node can hold yet. On a cluster that scales from zero, a pending pod is in effect the request for a new machine.
The open-source node autoscaler that AWS builds. It launches EC2 instances for pending pods and removes instances that are no longer needed.
The Karpenter object that says which instances Karpenter may launch, how many, and when it may remove them.
The Karpenter object that holds the AWS settings for a NodePool's nodes: the image, the IAM role, the subnets, the security groups, the disks and the reservations.
Karpenter's record of one instance on its way to becoming a node. It passes through the stages Launched, Registered and Initialized.
The purchase option that a NodePool allows: spot, on-demand or reserved, which means capacity reservations.
A taint is a mark on a node. Only pods that declare a matching toleration can be scheduled on a node that carries it.
The EC2 API that fills one capacity request from a list of instance types.
The Spot allocation strategy that takes the lowest-priced Spot pools among those with the most spare capacity.
Karpenter removing or replacing nodes to cut cost.
The state of a node that no longer matches its NodePool or its image. Karpenter replaces such a node.
The Amazon SQS queue through which Karpenter receives EC2 events, such as the Spot interruption warning.
A separate AWS tool that also reacts to EC2 events such as the Spot interruption warning. The EKS best-practices guide advises against running it alongside Karpenter's interruption handling.
An EC2 signal that a Spot Instance is at elevated risk of interruption. It can arrive before the two-minute interruption warning.
The signal that asks a process to stop. A pod receives it when it is evicted, and it then has its grace period to finish.
A Kubernetes add-on that queues jobs. It holds a Job until a quota has room and then lets the Job create its pods.
The Kueue object that describes one kind of node, such as Spot nodes, through node labels and tolerations.
The Kueue object that holds a quota for each flavor for the whole cluster.
The Kueue object that a team submits jobs to in its own namespace. It points at one ClusterQueue.
The unit that Kueue admits. Kueue creates one Workload for each Job.
A Kueue admission check that waits for capacity before it admits a Job. It is written for the Kubernetes cluster-autoscaler.
A group of Kueue ClusterQueues that lend each other unused quota.
A Kubernetes scheduler for GPU work. It adds hierarchical queues, gang scheduling and fractional GPUs.
Scheduling all of a job's pods together, or none of them.
A Kubernetes object that runs a group of Jobs as one unit and recreates them all when one fails.
The Kubeflow Trainer object that a user submits. It points at a runtime template that an administrator provides.
A DaemonSet that advertises a node's devices to Kubernetes. The NVIDIA device plugin advertises GPUs as nvidia.com/gpu.
A Kubernetes object that runs one pod on every matching node.
NVIDIA's package that installs the GPU driver, the toolkit, the device plugin, node labelling and monitoring together.
An NVIDIA feature that runs several processes on one GPU at the same moment.
A hardware feature that splits one GPU into isolated instances, each with its own memory and compute.
A way to share a GPU in which several pods take turns on the whole GPU, with no memory or compute isolation.
A Kubernetes API in which a driver publishes each device with its attributes and a pod claims a device by describing what it needs.
The EKS option in which AWS runs the node layer for you, including a managed Karpenter, the node image, the GPU driver and device plugin, Spot interruption handling and node repair.
The disk image that an EC2 instance boots from.
An operating system for EKS nodes. The EKS-optimized accelerated AL2023 image leaves the NVIDIA device plugin for you to install.
The AWS service whose sessions give shell access to an instance without SSH.
The EKS feature that acts on unhealthy node conditions. For GPUs, it acts on a double-bit memory error, an NVLink error and a critical XID error.
The NVIDIA driver's numbered report of a GPU fault.
NVIDIA's direct GPU-to-GPU connection.
The plug-in interface through which Kubernetes mounts a storage system into pods as volumes.

term: Mountpoint for Amazon S3 CSI driver
meaning: The CSI driver that presents an S3 bucket as a volume in a pod.
A way of providing volumes in which you write the volume definition for each existing storage resource, such as an S3 bucket, yourself.
A managed parallel file system for many nodes that read and write large files at the same time.
The EC2 network device that lets training processes on different nodes exchange data without going through the operating system's network stack.
A reservation that holds EC2 instances of one type for you.
A set of GPU instances booked in advance for a fixed window.
The EC2 GPU instance families whose names start with g, such as g5, g6, g6e and g7e.
A P6e machine that joins many GPUs with NVLink.
A number from 1 to 10 that says how likely a Spot request is to succeed in a Region or an Availability Zone.
The unit in which EC2 counts processor capacity and Spot quotas.
NVIDIA's workflow orchestrator for physical AI. In OSMO, one pipeline can run its tasks on training, simulation and edge computers.
The EKS feature that joins machines on your premises or at the edge to an EKS cluster as nodes, while AWS runs the control plane.
